MertensSecond

the sum of the reciprocals of the primes (Mertens' second theorem)
Proved in Leanring 1Survivor shares and analytic inputs

The sum of one over each prime up to x is log log x plus a constant plus a remainder at most a constant over log x (outside claim, from PNT+); so it is at most log log x plus a constant.

What it adds: Supplies the upper bound on the sum of prime reciprocals that Brun's choice of stopping point needs.

Claims (2)

mertens_second_remainder
proved in Lean
The sum of the prime reciprocals up to x is log log x plus a constant, with remainder at most a constant over log x, for x at least 2 (outside source; PNT+ Mertens.sum_prime_div_eq with Mertens.E₂p.abs_le, the two explicit constants replaced by some constant).
/-- **Mertens' second theorem, with its remainder** (outside claim, from PNT+). -/
def mertens_second_remainder : Prop :=
  ∃ M C : ℝ, ∀ x : ℝ, 2 ≤ x →
    |(∑ p ∈ Finset.Ioc 0 ⌊x⌋₊ with p.Prime, (1 : ℝ) / p) - Real.log (Real.log x) - M|
      ≤ C / Real.log x
Rests on: no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

prime_reciprocal_upper
proved in Lean
The sum of the prime reciprocals up to x is at most log log x plus a constant, for x at least 2.
/-- **The sum of the prime reciprocals is at most the logarithm of the
logarithm plus a constant.** -/
def prime_reciprocal_upper : Prop :=
  ∃ B : ℝ, 0 ≤ B ∧ ∀ x : ℝ, 2 ≤ x →
    (∑ p ∈ Finset.Ioc 0 ⌊x⌋₊ with p.Prime, (1 : ℝ) / p) ≤ Real.log (Real.log x) + B
Rests on: MertensSecond.mertens_second_remainder
